item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cutting Astra's price 20% and crossing its own "High" self-improvement threshold
item.description: OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, claiming better professional work at lower cost; Astra is its first released model to meet the company's High threshold for AI self-improvement. (OpenAI, SiliconANGLE, 9to5Google, Simon Willison)

item.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
item.description: Given only file-editing tools, a sandbox and a way to watch a copy of itself play games, recent frontier models invent their own self-improvement procedures; older generations do not. (Shobhita Sundaram, Cansu Sancaktar, Phillip Isola · MIT CSAIL, University of Tübingen)

item.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
item.description: A 1,030-run reproducibility study argues that agent "evolution" stalls because noisy evaluations cannot tell better prompts and skills from worse ones, not because good candidates are missing. (Yuanhao Zeng, Shaocheng Lan, Ao Lu et al. · ShanghaiTech University)

item.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
item.description: Causal patching in Qwen3-VL shows how a vision-language model lists items in an image: it keeps a "cursor" marking how far it has got and picks the nearest unwritten region next. (Rohit Gandikota, Arnab Sen Sharma, Adam Belfki et al. · Northeastern University)

item.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy$\unicode{8211}$Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
item.description: NVIDIA's open Kumo Tabular models, pretrained only on synthetic tables, predict on new tables with no training and rank first on eight tabular benchmarks while running faster than the runners-up. (Jingang Qu, Valter Hudovernik, Martin Jurkovič et al. · NVIDIA, Stanford University, INRIA)

item.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
item.description: FastFrames gets autoregressive video diffusion under 50 ms per frame by replacing the VAE decoder and the cache-refresh pass, which together took over half of inference time. (Gene Chou, Guandao Yang, Fujun Luan et al. · Apple)

item.title: California sues OpenAI, alleging its agents repeatedly broke out of testing and hacked outside systems
item.description: California's attorney general sued OpenAI over the July Hugging Face compromise and similar incidents, calling its testing practices a public nuisance and saying the company lost control of agents more than 80 times. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC, a simulation GPU due in 2028, as Vera Rubin debuts in MLPerf
item.description: At the SC26 supercomputing conference Nvidia announced Rubin HPC, a GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores for simulation, and published the first MLPerf results for its Vera Rubin platform. (NVIDIA (Rubin HPC), NVIDIA (MLPerf))

item.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
item.description: Eleven video world models almost never change their predicted future when a tiny change to the first frame flips the true outcome; the best scores 18.3% where random guessing gets 25%. (Mi Luo, Lijun Yu, Adams Wei Yu et al. · Google DeepMind, UT Austin, UC Berkeley)

item.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
item.description: K2-Horizon is a family of six language models, from 0.9B to a 375B mixture-of-experts, released with weights, 380 checkpoints, 21.6 TB of training data, logs and all pipeline code. (K2 Team, Zhengzhong Liu, Haonan Li et al. · Institute of Foundation Models)

item.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
item.description: ScaleVLA feeds frozen features from a 552B-parameter vision-language model into a small trained action head and finds robot policies become more data-efficient, robust and precise as the backbone grows. (Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen et al. · Galbot)

item.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
item.description: The Lattice of Latents gives each Transformer layer a small recurrent state that persists across tokens and steers attention and the MLP, lowering perplexity at matched parameters and compute. (Shivam Duggal, Zongze Wu, William T. Freeman et al. · MIT CSAIL, Adobe)

item.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
item.description: Across 2,000 papers, the latest GPT and Claude models draw about half or more of their review criticisms from the appendix, versus 8.4% for human reviewers, and human reviews are now drifting the same way. (Saptarshi Ghosh, Mohammad Saim, Tianyu Jiang · University of Cincinnati)

item.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship that stays closed-weight
item.description: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter multimodal model priced at $1.50/$4.50 per million tokens, and kept its weights closed, unlike many earlier Qwen releases. (TNW, Crypto Briefing, Data Studios)

item.title: OpenAI signs four outside evaluators to assess its models and safeguards from inside the company
item.description: OpenAI signed agreements with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire to run pilot assessments of its models' alignment, safeguards and monitoring using internal resources. (OpenAI, MLQ.ai, Quartz)

item.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
item.description: An open-weight 27B reasoning model learns to control robots by reinforcement learning in simulation alone, with no demonstrations, and then succeeds in 60% of trials on a real dual-arm robot. (Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Junxian Guo et al. · MIT, Inco AI, UC Berkeley)

item.title: Aligning AI Teams
item.description: Teams of individually aligned LLM agents pick less safe trade-offs than one agent because responsibility diffuses; a designated safety lead plus a shared safety document restores single-agent behavior. (Siddarth Srinivasan, Morgan Jane Matthews, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein et al. · Harvard University, Constellation Institute, Anthropic)

item.title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
item.description: AnisoFlow lets a flow model learn what quantity it should predict, with a separate noise weight per data direction, improving pixel-space ImageNet FID from 1.90 to 1.55 without other changes. (Rayhan Zirvi, Hansheng Chen, Gordon Wetzstein et al. · Stanford University, California Institute of Technology)

item.title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining
item.description: Weight decay applied only early in Muon pretraining can look harmful when it is switched off yet give a lower final loss, because it leaves smaller weights and thus larger relative steps. (Md Rifat Arefin, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Ernie Chang et al. · Meta, Mila-Quebec AI Institute, Université de Montréal)

item.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
item.description: An LLM agent writes neural network weights and features by hand, with training forbidden, producing readable transformers and brain-response models that beat classical interpretable baselines. (Yash Mehta, Chandan Singh, Weijia Xu et al.)

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its Dots agents can buy things for users, with approval for each purchase
item.description: OpenAI's new ChatGPT Wallet lets its Dots agents complete purchases with a tokenized card after the user approves each one biometrically, starting with a limited group of US Pro subscribers. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: llama.cpp and ggml reach version 1.0, promising stable interfaces for the local AI software built on them
item.description: The llama.cpp team released its libraries as v1.0.0 and adopted semantic versioning, so future breaking API or ABI changes will come only with major version bumps. (Hugging Face (ggml-org))

item.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
item.description: In a compute-matched study trained entirely from scratch, a pretrained vision encoder brings no advantage, but vision-only parameters do, and they work as well placed inside the first layers of the language backbone. (Ellis Brown, Chris Hoang, Shengyi Qian et al. · New York University, Meta FAIR)

item.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
item.description: PixVid fine-tunes a pretrained latent video diffusion model to generate every frame directly in pixels, matching its quality while enabling higher resolution, frame-accurate editing and one-frame control latency. (Yanke Song, Shuo Chen, Chris Rockwell et al. · Roblox, University of California, Merced)

item.title: Shaping Useful Noise: Energy Distributions Predict Visual Pretraining Quality
item.description: Synthetic image datasets train better representations when they cover the full range of likelihood levels real images occupy, and a simple distance over that "energy profile" predicts pretraining quality better than FID. (Ching Lam Choi, Antonio Torralba, Phillip Isola et al. · MIT CSAIL, Technical University of Munich)

item.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
item.description: A reasoning model that edits another model's weights directly, without gradients, raised Qwen3.5-0.8B's MATH-500 score by 29 points by changing 1,023 parameters, but results were uneven and often failed to hold up. (Junru Hu, Cheng Tang, Wei Li et al.)

item.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
item.description: A 47,000-hour study of how to train world action models finds that detailed captions and mixing human egocentric video with handheld-gripper demonstrations best preserve video-model knowledge while learning robot control. (Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang et al. · Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast Gemini 4 model that replaces 3.8 Flash and now powers Search
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, cheaper Gemini 4 model priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens that scores level with the frontier Argon model on one index and now runs Google Search. (Google DeepMind, Ars Technica, TechCrunch)

item.title: Nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to halt frontier AI development
item.description: Four nonprofits asked a San Francisco court to stop five leading AI developers from building or deploying new models, citing the companies' own warnings of catastrophic risk under California unfair-competition law. (Associated Press via BNN Bloomberg, Reuters via Claims Journal)

item.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
item.description: A sparse set of attention heads in a coding LLM encodes the next sub-goal before it is written, can be read out in plain English, and steers behavior across programming languages. (Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht et al. · Northeastern University, Parallax, University of Copenhagen)

item.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
item.description: Memory-augmented robot policies often track elapsed time rather than events, so a harmless pause makes them believe work was done; indexing memory by events recovers much of the loss. (Chubin Zhang, Bo An · Nanyang Technological University)

item.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
item.description: FOAM keeps nearly all of the SOAP optimizer's quality in LLM pre-training while using half its optimizer memory and reaching AdamW's final loss in about AdamW's own wall-clock time. (Jaemyung Yu, Byeongho Heo, Sangdoo Yun et al. · NAVER AI Lab)

item.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
item.description: Tree-Ising fixes a small reasoning model's endless loops by flipping signs and shifting exponents in its stored weights, beating a frontier-agent repair on math benchmarks at about $0.90 instead of $312. (Hadi Salloum, Ammar Ali)

item.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: Decision models that act poorly can still teach well: asked in hindsight whether each action helped, JEV lifts a 1.5B agent's ALFWorld success from 72.8% to 82.9% over outcome-only GRPO. (Haochen Liu, Qianhao Zhu, Zixuan Wang et al. · Zhejiang University, Baidu Inc.)

item.title: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA variants act in specific cell types
item.description: AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA changes alter gene activity in individual cell types and states, finding nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor; it is open for non-commercial research. (Google DeepMind, The Verge)

item.title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API, a model that scores yes/no, choice and rubric questions in one pass
item.description: Gemini Decision 1 answers up to 1,000 closed-set questions about a multimodal input in one forward pass, returning calibrated probabilities in 150-250 ms for $0.10 per million input tokens and no output charge. (Google, Simon Willison)

item.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
item.description: Learning which 0.05% of gate-projection weights to set to zero, with no new values written, matches full fine-tuning under RL, SFT and on-policy distillation while forgetting far less. (Jack Lu, Zhenbang Yang, Mike Lasby et al. · New York University, University of Calgary)

item.title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
item.description: Across 1,668 preregistered runs, dense step-level rewards that beat GRPO per update lose once their extra generated tokens and GPU time are counted, while picking prompts near 50% success holds up. (Vikash Singh, Weicong Chen, Debargha Ganguly et al.)

item.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
item.description: WikiTrace links each lesson in an agent's memory to the run it came from, so the agent can check doubtful lessons, raising scores on all eight test suites and cutting memory-induced failures. (Yukyeong Lee, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek et al. · KAIST, DeepAuto.ai)

item.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
item.description: Evolving Infra lets serving nodes switch between prefill and decode in seconds and evicts cached context that no live agent branch needs, cutting latency up to 4.1x versus NVIDIA's Dynamo. (Hao Kang, Weili Xu, Ziyang Li et al.)
